sup.16: The app says no device is connected
sup.17: Our apps can open drives Android itself can't, such as NTFS, ext4 or bootable drives. The phone still has to detect the drive. Work through this in order:
sup.18: Open your phone's Settings, search for OTG, and switch it on if the option exists.
sup.19: Check your adapter is a real data OTG adapter, not a charge-only cable. This is by far the most common cause.
sup.19b: When you plug the drive in, Android asks whether to let the app use the USB device. Tap OK. If you refused, unplug the drive and plug it in again. In Ultimate USB, DROFUS, Ventoy and USB Tools, also check the mode on the main screen is USB OTG, not SD Slot.
sup.20: Plug in a drive formatted as FAT32 or exFAT and check that Android notices it: most phones show a notification or a USB access prompt. Your phone's own file manager may not list NTFS or ext4 drives even when our apps can open them. If even a FAT32 drive isn't noticed, the problem is the cable, the port or the drive.
sup.21: Test the same drive on a PC to rule the drive out.
sup.22: Check the charging port for dust or lint.
sup.24: Most Android phones made in the last several years do. If searching Settings for OTG returns nothing, your phone most likely enables it automatically — the absence of a toggle isn't a sign it's unsupported. Confirm by plugging in a drive formatted as FAT32 or exFAT and checking your file manager.
sup.26: No — not for USB drives over OTG, which is what these apps are built for.
sup.27: Root is only needed to reach the phone's internal SD card slot, because Android doesn't expose it the same way. If you need to work on a microSD card without root, put it in a USB card reader and connect that over OTG instead.
sup.28: Can I use an external hard drive?
sup.29: Flash drives, card readers, portable SSDs and OTG hubs are supported. Mechanical external hard drives (HDDs) are not officially supported — they draw more power than a phone's USB port reliably provides, so they may fail to spin up or cut out mid-operation.
sup.30: If you try one anyway: charge the phone fully first, and use a powered USB hub if you have one.
sup.31: The drive disconnects part-way through an operation
sup.32: If the USB connection has a short failure during a job, the app recovers it automatically and the job continues, with no action from you.
sup.33: Don't move the phone or the cable while an operation is running — a fractionally loose adapter will disconnect on the smallest movement.
sup.34: Try a different OTG adapter. Cheap adapters fail under sustained load even when they work for a quick file copy.
sup.35: Keep the phone charged; a drive under sustained write load draws real power.
sup.36: Android says the drive is corrupted or unsupported after I format it
sup.37: That notification is expected after a drive is formatted as NTFS or ext2/3/4, and often after a bootable drive is written. It does not mean anything is wrong. Most Android devices have no built-in driver for these, so the system sees a drive it can't read and reports it as damaged or unsupported.
sup.38: The write succeeded. In Ultimate USB and Ventoy the drive still opens in USB File Manager.
sup.39: Dismiss the notification and never tap the option to format — that offer comes from Android, not from us, and it will erase the drive you just prepared.
sup.41: The ad won't load, or says “try again”
sup.42: This is the single most common report, and it's nearly always the network — not the app. In order of how often it's the fix:
sup.43: Private DNS. Open Settings, search for Private DNS, choose Private DNS provider hostname and enter dns.google. Save, toggle your connection off and on, then restart the app. Ad-blocking DNS providers block the ad servers, so no ad can load.
sup.44: Ad blockers and blocking VPNs. Disable them for the app. There is nothing to load through a blocker.
sup.45: Switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data. If ads load on one and not the other, the network is the cause.
sup.46: Watch the ad to the very end and close it with the X that appears. Pressing Back early cancels the reward.
sup.47: Why does the app need internet just to format a drive?
sup.48: The operation itself doesn't. The connection is for loading ads, which is what funds the free version — the ads are the price of the tools being free.
sup.49: If you want the apps to work fully offline, the one-time Pro upgrade removes ads and the token system entirely, and offline use comes with it.
sup.51: Tap the token counter on the main screen to open Get Tokens. Under Get 1 free token, tap Watch: one video ad of 60 seconds at most gives 1 token. Or buy Get 5 Tokens. Watching is free, up to a balance of 5 tokens and 4 ads each time you open the app.
sup.53: That's a limit, not a bug. Free tokens stop at a balance of 5, and the card then says You have enough tokens. Spend some and Watch comes back. After 4 ads in one session it says No more ads, restart app and try again. Close the app fully and open it again.
sup.55: Most tools are free. Only these cost tokens, and the number is always shown before you confirm:
sup.55a: ISO Burner (Ultimate USB, DROFUS): 2 for a Disk or ISO image copied file by file, such as a Windows ISO; 1 for Non-bootable, MS-DOS or FreeDOS. Images written as an exact copy (Raspberry Pi and other .img files, macOS DMG, and Linux ISOs unless you tick Advanced Options) are free.
sup.55d: Partition Wizard (Ultimate USB, USB Tools): 1 for each Create or Format step, at most 3 per Apply Changes.
sup.55e: PS2 USB Utils (Ultimate USB, USB Tools): 1 when Fix formats the drive.
sup.56: Everything else is free, including Wipe USB, Bad Blocks Check, Benchmark, Backup / Restore, USB Defragmenter, Raw Write, the file managers, Game Converter and adding PS2 games. If an operation fails, or the app closes before it finishes, the tokens are given back.
sup.57: I watched the ad but got no token
sup.58: The reward is granted when the ad reports completion, so it's lost if the ad is closed early or the connection drops mid-ad. Watch to the end, close with the X, and stay connected.
sup.59: If the ad definitely completed and the balance didn't move, force-stop the app (Settings → Apps → the app → Force stop) and reopen it while online.
sup.61: Token balances are stored on your device, not on an account. Uninstalling the app or clearing its data deletes them. They move to a new phone only if Android's own backup or phone transfer brings back the app's data.
sup.62: Pro is different — it's tied to your Google account and survives all of that.
sup.64: What does Pro actually give me?
sup.65: A one-time, lifetime purchase that removes all ads, removes the token system, and lets the app run fully offline and with ad blockers enabled. There is no subscription.
sup.66: To be precise about what it isn't: Pro removes the ads and the token requirement. It isn't a separate feature set — the tools themselves are the same.
sup.67: I bought Pro and it isn't showing
sup.68: Make sure the Play Store on this phone uses the same Google account that made the purchase. The apps have no sign-in of their own.
sup.69: Force-stop the app (Settings → Apps → the app → Force stop), then reopen it while online — the entitlement is confirmed with Google Play on launch.
sup.70: Check the purchase actually completed in the Play Store under Payments & subscriptions.
sup.71: If it still doesn't appear, email us with the Play Store order number.
sup.72: I bought tokens and they didn't arrive

sup.74: If they still aren't there, send us a screenshot of the app and a screenshot of the purchase in your Google Play payment history, and we'll sort it out.

sup.76: Yes. Pro follows the Google account, not the device. Install the app on the new phone with the same Google account in the Play Store, and Pro comes back when the app starts. Your token balance stays on the old phone unless Android's own backup or phone transfer brings back the app's data.

sup.78: Yes. Each app is a separate product on Google Play with its own purchase. If you want everything in one place, Ultimate USB contains the features of the individual tools.
sup.79: I can't complete a purchase in my country
sup.80: In-app purchases go through Google Play billing, and Play payment support varies by country — in some regions purchases are restricted regardless of the app. Nothing on our side can override that.
sup.81: Everything remains usable in the meantime: tokens are earned free by watching a rewarded ad, and no feature is locked behind payment alone.

sup.83: Google Play promo codes can only make an item completely free — there is no mechanism for a partial per-user discount, so we can't issue one.
sup.84: Every paid action is also reachable free by watching a rewarded ad, so nothing is locked behind payment.

sup.87: If the purchase failed to deliver, email us first with a screenshot of the app and of the Play purchase history — most cases turn out to be recoverable without a refund.
sup.89: No. These apps rely on low-level USB and storage access that iOS doesn't provide. Android only, and a purchase on Android doesn't carry to any other platform.
sup.91: Which file system should I choose?
sup.92: FAT32 — maximum compatibility (TVs, car stereos, consoles, BIOS boot). Single files are limited to 4 GB.
sup.93: exFAT — no practical file-size limit, still read by phones, Windows and macOS. The best default for general use.
sup.94: NTFS — for Windows. No practical file-size limit, but most Android phones can't read it.
sup.95: ext2/3/4 — for Linux. Neither Android nor Windows reads it without extra software.
sup.95b: Ultimate USB and USB Tools offer all of these in Format USB. DROFUS offers FAT32, exFAT and NTFS for a Non-bootable drive, and Ventoy offers FAT32, exFAT and NTFS for its drive.
sup.96: I formatted to NTFS (or ext4) and now my phone can't read the drive
sup.97: The format succeeded. The limitation is Android itself: most Android devices have no built-in NTFS or ext2/3/4 support, so the system can't mount the drive even though a PC will read it perfectly. A handful of manufacturers add NTFS support, but it is the exception rather than the rule.
sup.98: Ultimate USB and Ventoy still open the drive in USB File Manager.
sup.99: If you need the drive readable by the phone's own file manager and other apps, use exFAT. It has no practical file-size limit and is read by Android, Windows and macOS alike.
sup.100: Format failed, or the verification check failed
sup.101: Confirm the adapter is a data OTG adapter and reseat it.
sup.102: Test the drive on a PC — a drive that fails verification usually has failing flash.
sup.103: Try a different USB port on the adapter or a different adapter entirely.
sup.104: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, run Bad Blocks Check to confirm whether the flash itself is at fault. It erases the drive.
sup.105: A verification failure means the drive did not keep the data written to it. That is a hardware symptom, and no app can format around it.
sup.106: The drive shows less capacity than it should
sup.107: Two ordinary causes and one bad one:
sup.108: Manufacturers count in decimal gigabytes; your phone counts in binary. A "64 GB" drive genuinely holds about 59 GiB.
sup.109: A previous bootable write may have left hidden partitions. Recover the space with Partition Wizard or Format USB in Ultimate USB and USB Tools, by writing the drive with Non-bootable in DROFUS, or with Clear in Ventoy.
sup.110: If the shortfall is large, the drive may be counterfeit. All four apps test the drive when it is connected and, if reading or writing at its end fails, ask whether to Scan for real size or Continue anyway.
sup.111: How do I get back unallocated space?
sup.112: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, open Partition Wizard, select the unallocated block and tap Create, or Delete the existing partitions and create one across the drive. Your changes are listed for review, then Apply Changes runs them together.
sup.113: The quickest route, if you don't need what's on the drive: Format USB in Ultimate USB and USB Tools, or Non-bootable in DROFUS.
sup.115: GPT for modern UEFI machines. MBR for older BIOS/legacy boot, and for consoles like the PS2 that require it.
sup.116: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, Partition Wizard converts between them without a PC (Convert Partition Table). In DROFUS and Ventoy you choose the Partition Table: before writing. Back the drive up first regardless — any change to a partition table is a change you don't want to get halfway through.
sup.118: Which app should I use to make a bootable drive?
sup.119: DROFUS — one ISO, maximum control over the result. The straightforward choice for a Windows or Linux installer.
sup.120: Ventoy (Unofficial) — install once, then drag as many ISOs onto the drive as it holds and pick at boot. Best if you carry several installers.
sup.121: Ultimate USB — contains both, plus partitioning, diagnostics and the rest.
sup.122: The drive was created but the PC won't boot from it
sup.123: The write can be perfect and the PC still refuse it. Check, in this order:
sup.124: Boot menu. Actually select the USB drive in the boot menu (usually F12, F11, F9 or Esc at power-on) rather than expecting it to boot on its own.
sup.125: Secure Boot. Disable it in the BIOS/UEFI, or use a build that supports it.
sup.126: Partition scheme. GPT drives need UEFI mode; MBR drives need legacy/CSM. A mismatch means the drive simply won't appear.
sup.127: USB port. Try a rear port directly on the motherboard, not a front-panel or hub port.
sup.128: The ISO itself. Re-download it if it came from anywhere other than the official source — a truncated ISO writes fine and boots into nothing.
sup.129: My Windows ISO has a file bigger than 4 GB
sup.130: That's install.wim, and FAT32 can't hold it. In Ultimate USB and DROFUS, tick Split image for FAT32 compatibility. to split it into .swm parts so the drive can stay FAT32, which modern Secure Boot PCs usually need. Windows setup puts the parts back together; nothing is lost. Splitting takes a long time.
sup.131: Without the tick the app uses NTFS, which has no size limit but isn't accepted by every UEFI firmware. On a Ventoy drive the ISO is copied as one file, so use exFAT or NTFS there.
sup.132: How do I switch Ventoy between MBR and GPT?
sup.133: In Ventoy, or in Ultimate USB under Ventoy - Unofficial, choose MBR or GPT under Partition Table:, then tap Install. You don't need a PC.
sup.134: Install wipes the drive completely, including any ISOs already copied to it, so copy them back afterwards with Copy File To USB. Update keeps your ISOs but doesn't change the partition table.
sup.135: How do I add or remove ISOs on a Ventoy drive?
sup.136: In Ultimate USB and Ventoy, once Ventoy is installed, add ISOs with Copy File To USB, or save them straight to the drive with Download File Directly To USB FROM INTERNET. Copying them on a PC works too. No reburning, no reinstalling. Delete an ISO in USB File Manager and it leaves the boot menu.
sup.137: What is Linux persistence, and why is the option greyed out?
sup.138: Persistence keeps your files and changes on the USB drive across reboots of a live Linux system. In Ultimate USB and DROFUS, tick Advanced Options (Filesystem, Partition & Persistence), then set Persistent partition size. The app adds an ext3 or ext4 partition for it.
sup.139: It's offered only for images that support it. For the others the app says why: the image doesn't support it, the distribution sets it up itself, or the image is written sector by sector. It also needs enough free space on the drive. On a Ventoy drive, use Add persistence in Config Hub (Ultimate USB, Ventoy).
sup.141: In Ultimate USB and DROFUS, choosing Windows To Go instead of Standard Windows Installation puts a full Windows installation on the USB drive itself, rather than an installer for a PC. It can take several hours: use a fast drive, a fast phone and High-speed mode., and start with a full battery.
sup.142: Can I burn a macOS DMG or a Raspberry Pi image?
sup.143: Yes, in Ultimate USB and DROFUS (ISO Burner, Disk or ISO image), with no token cost. macOS DMG (Intel-based), Raspberry Pi OS and other ARM images are written as raw blocks, preserving the original layout and boot structure. There's no customisation applied to these, by design.
sup.145: The operation is stuck or won't finish
sup.146: Three causes cover almost every case:
sup.147: The app was minimised. Operations pause when the app leaves the foreground — that's deliberate, to protect the drive from a half-finished write. Keep it on screen and keep the screen awake.
sup.148: The adapter or drive. Reseat the adapter, don't move the phone while it runs, and try another adapter if it recurs. A loose or charge-only adapter is the usual culprit.
sup.148b: No internet or an ad blocker (free version). The app shows No Internet Connection or Adblocker or Private DNS detected., and running operations wait until that's fixed. Pro doesn't pause for either.
sup.149: Large drives and large images simply take time — a write that looks frozen on a slow drive is often still progressing. If the progress figure hasn't moved at all for a long stretch, treat it as a stall and check the two points above.
sup.150: It stalls near the very end — 99%, or in the last few percent
sup.151: The end of a write is where data reaches the far end of the drive. Stalling there is the classic signature of a drive that reports more capacity than it physically has, or whose flash is failing at the far end.
sup.152: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, run Bad Blocks Check with Detect fake / counterfeit capacity ticked (it erases the drive). In DROFUS and Ventoy, reconnect the drive: if the end of the drive fails the test, the app asks whether to Scan for real size or Continue anyway. If the drive is bad, no app can fix it.
sup.153: Can the app damage my USB drive?
sup.154: No. Nothing the app does is unrecoverable at the hardware level — the worst case is a drive that needs formatting again. If a drive stopped working after an operation, it was already failing.
sup.155: Can I use my phone while an operation runs?
sup.156: Not on other apps — operations pause when the app is minimised. Leave it in the foreground until it finishes. Long operations on large drives can take a while, so start them when you don't need the phone.
sup.157: The app crashed or closed by itself
sup.158: First check you installed from Google Play. Modified or repackaged copies from APK sites are a common source of crashes we can't reproduce or fix.
sup.159: If it's the Play version, write to us with the app version, your phone model, the drive size and file system, and what you were doing when it closed. Crashes we can reproduce get fixed quickly.
sup.161: How do I tell if a drive is counterfeit?
sup.162: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, run Bad Blocks Check with Detect fake / counterfeit capacity ticked. It tests the whole drive, so it erases everything on it. A counterfeit drive reports a large capacity but silently discards anything past its real size, which the test exposes. All four apps also test the drive when it is connected and, if reading or writing at its end fails, ask whether to Scan for real size or Continue anyway.
sup.163: Symptoms before you test: files that copy successfully but are corrupt afterwards, and writes that stall near the end.
sup.164: Can a corrupted drive be repaired?
sup.165: Logical corruption, such as a broken partition table or file system, is usually fixed by formatting fresh: Format USB or Wipe USB in Ultimate USB and USB Tools, Non-bootable in DROFUS, or Install in Ventoy. The apps don't repair a drive in place, so copy off what you need first.
sup.166: Physical flash failure isn't repairable by any software. If Bad Blocks Check (Ultimate USB, USB Tools) reports errors, replace the drive.
sup.167: Does Wipe USB really erase everything?
sup.168: Wipe USB (Ultimate USB, USB Tools) overwrites the whole drive once, which matches the "Clear" level in NIST SP 800-88 and defeats all normal file-recovery software. Choose Sampled (recommended) or Full verification to have it read the drive back, and save the erasure report and certificate when it finishes.
sup.169: It is not a multi-pass or "Purge"-level erase, and we don't claim it is. For legally mandated destruction standards, follow your own policy.
sup.170: My drive is slower than advertised
sup.171: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, run Benchmark for real numbers. Bear in mind the whole chain limits speed: a USB 3.0 drive in a USB 2.0 adapter runs at USB 2.0 speed, and advertised figures are usually peak read, not sustained write.
sup.172: Small-file writes are always dramatically slower than large sequential ones. That's how flash works, not a fault.
sup.174: How do I set up a drive for PS2 / OPL?
sup.175: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, open PS2 USB Utils. If the drive isn't FAT32 or exFAT with an MBR partition table, tap Fix to prepare it (1 token, erases the drive). Then add games with Import & Split ISO. On FAT32, games of 4 GB or more are converted to USBExtreme (.ul) and ul.cfg is updated. Other games can use Direct Copy - Recommended.
sup.176: OPL needs unfragmented game files. If a game shows Fragmented, tap Defragment. If that can't finish, use Run Full Defragmenter.
sup.177: Which game formats can be converted?
sup.178: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, Game Converter converts between ISO, BIN/CUE, VCD, ZSO, CSO and CHD, in the directions each format supports. Compressing to ZSO or CSO saves considerable space at a small performance cost.
sup.179: Do you supply the games, BIOS files, or console firmware?
sup.180: No. The apps are tools for organising files you already own. We don't bundle, host or distribute game images, BIOS files, console firmware or any proprietary console component. PlayStation 1 games on a PS2 drive need a system file in /POPS/ that you must supply yourself.
sup.182: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, Download Game Arts fetches artwork online, so it needs a working connection. Games with an unusual or renamed game ID may have no artwork available to match.
sup.185: It's been retired. Every feature it had is in DROFUS, along with everything added since — install that instead.
sup.186: Which app do I need if I only want one?
sup.187: Ultimate USB. It contains the bootable-USB writer, Ventoy, formatting, partitioning, diagnostics, backup and the console-game tools in one app. The separate apps exist for people who want just one job done.
sup.188: Do my files get uploaded anywhere?
sup.189: No. Your files are processed on your device, and their contents are never uploaded to us. What each app does send, such as crash reports and purchase checks, is set out in that app's own privacy policy; each app links to it in its menu, and all of them are listed on our privacy page.
sup.190: Do the apps create an account?
sup.191: No. There's no sign-up, no profile and no account to delete. Pro is tied to your Google Play purchase, which Google manages, and tokens live on your device.
sup.192: How do I restore a backup, or open a .bk file?
sup.193: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, open Backup / Restore and tap Restore to write a .bk backup back to a drive. To look inside one without restoring it, open the .bk file in Ultimate USB's Partition Image Manager.
sup.194: Is the app available in my language?

sup.ch.3: ChaoMe: what does Theme check do?

sup.ch.9: ChaoMe: how do I change the app's language?
sup.ch.10: Use Settings → Language. ChaoMe is available in English, Hindi, Indonesian, Russian and Simplified Chinese, and System default follows your phone's language.
sup.ch.11: ChaoMe: what does PRO add, and how do I restore it?

sup.ch.14: Open Settings → Privacy. Where your region requires it, Ad and data choices reopens the consent form, and in US states with an opt-out right Do not sell or share my personal information stops personalised ads. With PRO, Settings → Privacy shows only the privacy policy. See the ChaoMe privacy policy.
sup.ch.15: ChaoMe: why does the free version need the internet?

sup.ch.18: Since Android 11, apps can't read the installed-themes folder by themselves. Install Shizuku, start it and tap Allow when ChaoMe asks (on a rooted phone, Shizuku can be started with root). The themes appear the next time ChaoMe starts.
sup.ch.19: ChaoMe: how do I move my theme library to a new phone?
sup.ch.20: In the Theme library, tap Back up to save a zip file, copy it to the new phone and tap Restore there. PRO comes back from Google Play by itself.

sup.cl.4: How do I back up my vault or move it to a new phone?
sup.cl.5: Copy the vault file with any file manager. With Pro, Settings → Back up copies it to a folder you choose in one tap and reminds you while the phone is charging. A vault kept inside the app can't be reached by a file manager: copy it with Settings → Copy file (free) or Back up (Pro).

sup.cl.7: Vault file names start with a dot, so in the file picker open the menu and choose Show hidden files.
sup.cl.8: The copy stays fully encrypted wherever you keep it.
sup.cl.9: What happens if I uninstall the app?
sup.cl.10: A vault file in a location you chose stays where you put it. After reinstalling, open the vault file again and turn fingerprint unlock back on. The app's settings and vault list start fresh.
sup.cl.12: Fingerprint unlock works per vault, on Android 9 and later with a strong fingerprint sensor. Your password always stays the master key. If you add or remove fingerprints in Android, unlock with the password and turn fingerprint unlock on again in Settings. It works with strong (Class 3) biometrics only; most phones' face unlock is not strong enough and is not offered.
sup.cl.13: Where are my files, and how much can a vault hold?
sup.cl.14: Your files are encrypted inside the vault file: at the location you chose, or in Cofferlock's own folder if you picked Keep it inside the app (Settings then shows Inside Cofferlock (hidden from file managers)). Nothing is uploaded. Any file type can go in. A free vault holds up to 5 GB; with Pro the only limit is your storage. Photos and videos open in your usual apps through Open or Share.
sup.cl.15: I deleted a file by mistake
sup.cl.16: In the free version, deleting is secure and immediate, so the file can't be brought back. Pro can keep a Trash for 7 or 30 days; once the Trash is emptied, the files are gone for good.
sup.cl.17: Pro or Supporter, and how do I restore a purchase?
sup.cl.18: Both are one-time purchases with the same features; Supporter simply costs more to support development. Your purchase follows your Google account: use Settings → About → Restore purchase.
sup.cl.19: Can you open or recover my vault?
sup.cl.20: No. We can't see, open or decrypt a vault, and there is no backdoor. A vault erased by Emergency erase or by Erase after wrong passwords is gone permanently.
sup.cl.22: The app lists this itself under Settings → About → What this app does not protect against. In short: it can't protect a vault on a rooted or compromised phone while it is unlocked, a weak password, files you have exported or shared, or someone filming your screen.
sup.cl.24: Only to check for app updates, to confirm purchases with Google Play and, if your phone's automatic date and time is off, to read the time from a public time server. Vaults open offline. Your files, passwords and recovery phrase never leave your phone. See the Cofferlock privacy policy.

sup.cl.26: Can I import or copy out a whole folder?

sup.cl.28: The app says my vault file is damaged

sup.cl.35: Pro turns on once Google Play confirms the purchase, which needs an internet connection once. Wait a moment, or use Settings → About → Restore purchase. If it still fails, contact us with a screenshot of your Play purchase history.
sup.cl.36: How do I send a file securely?
sup.cl.37: Select it and choose Send as sealed envelope (Pro). It becomes a small vault file with its own password; send it through any app and tell the password in person. Whoever receives it opens it with Cofferlock for free. Nothing goes through our servers.
sup.cl.38: Can I add files from another app?
sup.cl.39: With Pro, Cofferlock appears in every app's Share menu. Share photos or files to it, unlock, and tap Add; the app then tells you how many files are now encrypted in the vault. In the free version, add files from inside the app with the + button.
sup.fm.1: USB File Manager doesn't see my drive
sup.fm.2: Switch on OTG in your phone's settings if the option exists. Some phones switch it off again after a while.
sup.fm.3: Try another OTG adapter or cable. Charge-only adapters can't carry data.
sup.fm.4: For hard disks, use a powered USB hub: a phone often can't supply enough power on its own.
sup.fm.5: Check the drive on a computer, then unplug it and plug it in again.
sup.fm.6: Android asks to allow access to the USB device
sup.fm.7: Tap Allow. The app can only open the drive after you allow it. If you closed the prompt, tap Allow access on the drive's card, or unplug the drive and plug it in again. If opening fails, tap Try again.
sup.fm.8: Can I write to NTFS drives?
sup.fm.9: Yes, NTFS drives are fully readable and writable. A drive opens read-only only when Windows hibernated it (Fast Startup), when Windows did not close it cleanly and it could not be repaired, or when the drive is write-protected or refuses writes. Shut Windows down fully (not Restart or Sleep), or check the drive in Windows, then connect it again.
sup.fm.10: Copying a file larger than 4 GB fails
sup.fm.11: That is a limit of the FAT32 file system, not of the app: FAT32 can't store a single file over 4 GB. Use a drive formatted as exFAT or NTFS for large files.
sup.fm.12: Can USB File Manager format a drive?
sup.fm.13: No. USB File Manager browses and manages files; it has no formatting, partitioning or disk-image tools. To format, partition or repair a drive, use USB Tools or Ultimate USB.
sup.fm.15: Not for USB drives. Root is only needed for the phone's internal SD card slot, and your root manager (such as Magisk or KernelSU) must allow the app.
sup.fm.16: How do I unplug the drive safely?
sup.fm.17: Wait for any running operation to finish, then tap Eject on the drive's card. When it says Safe to unplug, pull the drive out. If something could not be saved, the app tells you to check the drive on a computer. Unplugging during a copy can damage the files being written.
sup.fm.18: I bought Pro and it isn't active
sup.fm.19: Pro is a one-time purchase tied to your Google account. Open ⋮ → Go Pro: remove ads (or Settings → Remove ads) and tap Restore purchases while online. If it still isn't active, check that the Play Store is signed in with the account that bought it and that the payment isn't still pending. Pro removes all ads, the No Internet Connection pause and the ad-blocker notice, and once confirmed it works offline for up to 30 days at a time.
sup.fm.20: The app says it is out of date
sup.fm.21: When the app shows Update Required, tap UPDATE NOW to open its Google Play page. If the update isn't mandatory you can tap LATER. If it is, there is no LATER button and the app closes after a few seconds until it is updated.
sup.fm.22: Which file systems and drives work?
sup.fm.23: FAT12, FAT16, FAT32, exFAT, NTFS and ext2/3/4, all readable and writable, on flash drives, card readers, hard disks and SSDs (through a powered hub if needed). Drives with several partitions (MBR or GPT) show each one by its label, or as Partition 1, Partition 2 and so on when it has none, and you can open several drives and partitions at once in tabs.
sup.fm.24: The app warns that my drive may store less than its size says
sup.fm.25: That is typical of counterfeit drives, which report more space than they really have. Files written beyond the real capacity can be lost, so don't keep your only copy of important files on that drive.
sup.fm.26: How do I change my ad choices in USB File Manager?
sup.fm.27: Where your region requires it, open ⋮ → Settings → Help & about → Privacy Settings to reopen the consent form. Pro has no ads at all. See the USB File Manager privacy policy.
sup.fm.28: It says an ad blocker was detected
sup.fm.29: While an operation runs, the free version pauses if ads are blocked by an ad-blocker app, Private DNS or your network. Turn the blocker off, or set Private DNS to dns.google, then restart the app. Pro works with ad blockers.
sup.fm.30: How do I open or share a file with another app?
sup.fm.31: Tap the file, or use Open with… or Share (up to 16 files). The file is read straight from the drive. With Open with… the app you choose can also save changes back to it; a shared file can only be read.
sup.fm.32: How do I copy files between my phone and the drive?
sup.fm.33: In a folder, tap Add → Import File / Files or Import Directory. To copy to the phone, select files and use Copy to… or Export. The phone side always goes through Android's folder picker.
sup.fm.34: How do I clear the Recent list or rename my drive?
sup.fm.35: Recent tab → Clear history; the list stays on your phone and is not backed up. To rename a drive, open it and use ⋮ → Rename label.

sup.tt.1: Is TumTum free? Are there in-app purchases?
sup.tt.2: TumTum is free and supported by ads, and it has no in-app purchases. Every level is unlocked simply by playing.
sup.tt.3: How do I get coins and hints?
sup.tt.4: You earn coins by solving levels for the first time (more for more stars and for 3-star streaks) and from a chest at the end of every fifth chapter. A hint costs 10 coins. If you tap Hint without enough coins and a video is available, you can choose Watch an ad to earn 15 coins. Watching is always optional.
sup.tt.6: Every level is checked by a solver to make sure it has a solution, and the move limit is based on the best one. One swipe moves every character until it hits something, so the order of your swipes matters. Pits and spikes are one-way, and only Undo brings a character back. Use Undo or Restart freely, or tap Hint.
sup.tt.8: Yes. Every level plays fully offline. Ads and the optional videos for extra coins need a connection.
sup.tt.9: My progress is gone, or I changed phones
sup.tt.10: Progress, stars and coins are saved on your device. There is no account and no cloud save, so clearing the game's data or uninstalling it resets your progress. If Android backup is on, reinstalling on the same phone may bring it back, but progress can't be moved to a different phone model.
sup.tt.11: How do I turn off personalized ads or crash reports?
sup.tt.12: Open Settings → Privacy in the game. Tap Personalised ads • On to turn personalisation off (with US English it's shown as Do not sell or share my personal information). Where your region requires it, Ad and data choices reopens the consent form. Switch Crash reports off or on there too. See the TumTum privacy policy for the details.
sup.tt.13: Why don't I see the “Watch an ad” option?
sup.tt.14: It appears only when you tap Hint without enough coins and a video has loaded. You need a connection, and in regions that require consent, ads stay off until you answer the privacy prompt. You can change your answer in Settings → Privacy → Ad and data choices.
sup.tt.15: How do I turn off sound, music or vibration?
sup.tt.16: Open Settings → Sound & vibration in the game. Sound, music and vibration each have their own switch, and sound and music have a volume slider.
sup.tt.17: Can I change the game's language?
sup.tt.18: Yes. TumTum is available in 11 languages and follows your phone's language by default. To choose another, open Settings → Language in the game; pick System default to follow the phone again.
sup.tt.19: Does TumTum need an account or upload anything?
sup.tt.20: No. There's no account or sign-up, and the game handles none of your files. It sends only ad requests and, if switched on, crash reports. See the TumTum privacy policy.
sup.u.1: Do I lose tokens if an operation fails?
sup.u.2: No. If an operation fails, or the app closes before it finishes, the tokens it cost are given back, at the latest the next time you open the app.
sup.u.3: Why did everything pause with “No Internet Connection”?
sup.u.4: The free version needs a connection for its ads. While you're offline it shows No Internet Connection, and running operations wait. Nothing is lost: they continue on their own once you're back online. Pro works fully offline.
sup.u.5: It says “Adblocker or Private DNS detected.”
sup.u.6: The free version can't load ads through an ad blocker, a blocking VPN or ad-blocking Private DNS. Running operations wait until it's switched off for the app. Set Private DNS to dns.google or turn it off, then restart the app. Pro, or any token pack you've bought on this install, lets the app run with an ad blocker on.
sup.u.7: Why does it ask me to solve a sum before buying?
sup.u.8: That's Parental Verification. If Google Play reports that the account belongs to a teenager, a purchase needs a parent's check first. For younger users, and for supervised accounts whose approval is pending or was declined, purchases are off.
sup.u.9: How do I change my ad and privacy choices?
sup.u.10: Tap the ? (Help) button on the main screen. Where your region requires it, Privacy Settings reopens the consent form, where you can change or withdraw consent and, in US states with an opt-out right, opt out of the sale or sharing of your data. Privacy Policy in the same menu opens the app's policy: Ultimate USB, DROFUS, Ventoy, USB Tools. Pro shows no ads at all.
sup.u.11: Can other apps open the files on my USB drive?
sup.u.12: In Ultimate USB, Partition Mounter mounts a partition as Read Only or Read / Write; tap Open Files App and other apps can open it through Android's file picker. Unmount it before unplugging. In Ultimate USB and Ventoy, opening a file in USB File Manager lets you choose another app to open it straight from the drive.
sup.u.13: Can I work on a disk image file instead of a drive?
sup.u.14: In Ultimate USB, Partition Image Manager opens or creates a partition image file (Create Partition Image .img) and lets you browse and edit it like a drive. Raw Write writes an image file to a drive byte by byte. DROFUS, Ventoy and USB Tools work on drives only.
sup.u.15: I forgot the password of an encrypted drive
sup.u.16: It can't be recovered or reset; that's what protects the files. In Ultimate USB, USB Encryption can only make the drive usable again by formatting it, which erases everything. While you still know the password, Change Password changes it quickly.
sup.u.17: How do I use the phone's SD card slot?
sup.u.18: It needs a rooted phone. Choose SD Slot instead of USB OTG on the main screen, tap Grant and accept your root manager's prompt, then Mount. Without root, put the card in a USB card reader and use USB OTG.
sup.u.19: What does “CRITICAL WARNING: BAD DRIVE!” mean?
sup.u.20: When a drive is connected, the app tests it. 🛑 CRITICAL WARNING: BAD DRIVE! means the drive dropped out or stopped answering during this test: the drive may be faulty, the cable loose, or the drive counterfeit. Try another cable or drive. If only the end of the drive fails, the app instead asks whether to Scan for real size or Continue anyway; after a scan, tap Yes to use only the part that works.
sup.u.21: What do the Windows setup options do?
sup.u.22: In Ultimate USB and DROFUS, Windows Setup Customization changes the installer you write. It can remove the TPM 2.0, Secure Boot and 4 GB RAM checks, drop the online Microsoft account requirement, create a local account (Windows asks for its password at first sign-in), skip the privacy questions, copy regional settings from your phone and turn off automatic BitLocker encryption. Nothing you enter leaves the phone. On a Ventoy drive, Config Hub has Windows 11: bypass hardware checks and Windows 11: bypass online account instead.
sup.u.23: Can I theme or password-protect a Ventoy drive?
sup.u.24: Yes, in Ultimate USB and Ventoy. Theme Manager imports a GRUB2 theme archive onto the drive, and Get more themes opens a theme website in your browser. Config Hub sets a boot-menu password, menu options and persistence. These settings are written only to the drive.
sup.u.25: How do I get an erasure certificate?
sup.u.26: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, run Wipe USB. When it finishes, tap View erasure report or View erasure certificate and save it. It can't be produced again later. The certificate is made on your phone and goes nowhere unless you share it.

tl.backup-restore.1: How do I back up a drive?
tl.backup-restore.2: Connect the drive to your phone with a USB OTG adapter and open Ultimate USB or USB Tools.
tl.backup-restore.3: Open the Disk Management group and tap Backup / Restore.
tl.backup-restore.4: Tap Backup and pick the folder where the backup goes.
tl.backup-restore.5: The whole drive is saved as one file named ultimate_backup_ plus a number, with the extension .bk.
tl.backup-restore.6: The backup file is as large as the whole drive. If the folder has too little space, the app shows Not Enough Space. If the folder cannot be opened, it shows Error opening output directory. A file over 4 GB cannot be saved to a FAT32 drive, and the app tells you so.
tl.backup-restore.7: How do I restore a backup?
tl.backup-restore.8: Connect the drive and open Backup / Restore.
tl.backup-restore.10: The app shows All Data Will Be Permanently Deleted. Confirm, and the file is written to the drive.
tl.backup-restore.11: The drive must be at least as big as the backup file.
tl.backup-restore.12: To look inside a .bk file without restoring it, open it in Ultimate USB's Partition Image Manager. To back up one partition instead of the whole drive, use Backup in Partition Wizard.
tl.backup-restore.13: How many tokens does a backup or restore use?
tl.backup-restore.14: None. Backup and Restore are free.
tl.backup-restore.15: What if I stop it or unplug the drive?
tl.backup-restore.16: To stop, tap cancel and confirm Are you sure you want to cancel the process?
tl.backup-restore.17: A cancelled backup deletes its unfinished file.
tl.backup-restore.18: A cancelled restore leaves the drive only partly written.
tl.backup-restore.19: If the drive is unplugged or stops answering, the app shows Device Removed with Retry. Plug the same drive back in and tap Retry: the backup or restore continues where it stopped. A different drive is never written.
tl.backup-restore.20: Is Backup / Restore safe for my drive?
tl.backup-restore.21: Yes. A restore waits until the drive confirms the data is written before the app reports success, and it protects the drive at each step:
tl.backup-restore.22: Restore refuses a drive that is write-protected or does not take writes up front, with one message, before any question or file pick.
tl.backup-restore.23: If the drive did not keep its test data, it may be fake. The app says so, keeps its files read-only and offers Try restore again. Restore still runs after an extra Yes.
tl.backup-restore.24: A job never writes to a different drive than the one it started on.
tl.backup-restore.25: If the USB connection fails for a moment during a job, the app recovers it automatically and the job continues.
tl.backup-restore.26: More than five years of building USB apps, and over 1,000,000 downloads each on Google Play for Ultimate USB and USB Tools.
tl.backup-restore.27: Read more: How our USB apps keep your drive and your data safe.
tl.backup-restore.desc: Open Backup / Restore in Ultimate USB or USB Tools. Backup saves a full byte-by-byte copy of the drive as a .bk file in a folder you pick. Restore writes a .bk file back to a drive. Both use no tokens.

tl.bad-blocks-check.1: How do I check a drive for bad blocks step by step?
tl.bad-blocks-check.2: Copy any files you want to keep off the drive. The check destroys all data on it.
tl.bad-blocks-check.3: Connect the drive to your phone with a USB OTG adapter and open Ultimate USB or USB Tools.
tl.bad-blocks-check.4: Open the Diagnostics & Info group and tap Bad Blocks Check.
tl.bad-blocks-check.5: Number of Passes: choose 1 Pass or 2 Passes.
tl.bad-blocks-check.6: Keep Detect fake / counterfeit capacity ticked to test the real size of the drive.
tl.bad-blocks-check.7: Tap START. The app warns that all data will be destroyed. Confirm to start.
tl.bad-blocks-check.8: Keep the app in the foreground while the check runs: operations pause when the app is minimized, to protect the drive.
tl.bad-blocks-check.9: Which options can I set, and what are the defaults?
tl.bad-blocks-check.19: What does Bad Blocks Check find?
tl.bad-blocks-check.20: Failing sectors: places on the drive that do not keep data correctly are reported as bad blocks.
tl.bad-blocks-check.21: Fake-capacity drives: a counterfeit USB drive or SD card reports a large capacity but silently discards anything past its real size. The check exposes this.
tl.bad-blocks-check.22: What do I do if the check finds errors?
tl.bad-blocks-check.23: Replace the drive. Physical flash failure cannot be repaired by any software.
tl.bad-blocks-check.24: Does Bad Blocks Check use tokens?
tl.bad-blocks-check.25: No. Bad Blocks Check is free. The app only asks you to confirm before it starts.
tl.bad-blocks-check.26: To measure the drive's speed without erasing it, use Benchmark with Read Only.
tl.bad-blocks-check.27: A drive that is write-protected or does not take writes is refused before the app asks you anything.
tl.bad-blocks-check.28: When you connect a drive that may be fake, the app also asks whether to Scan for real size or Continue anyway.
tl.bad-blocks-check.desc: Open Bad Blocks Check in Ultimate USB or USB Tools, choose 1 or 2 passes and tap START. It finds failing sectors and fake-capacity drives, and uses no tokens. It erases all data on the drive.

tl.benchmark.1: How do I run a speed test step by step?
tl.benchmark.2: Connect the drive to your phone with a USB OTG adapter and open Ultimate USB or USB Tools.
tl.benchmark.3: Open the Diagnostics & Info group and tap Benchmark.

tl.benchmark.17: Why is my drive slower than the speed on the box?

tl.benchmark.21: To check whether the flash itself is failing, run Bad Blocks Check. It erases the drive.
tl.benchmark.22: Benchmark does not change your files, in either mode. Results are shown in MB/s.
tl.benchmark.23: If the drive gives inconsistent results, the test stops.

tl.file-manager.3: Open the File & Storage group and tap USB File Manager.
tl.file-manager.4: The app shows Waiting For USB Device… and then Reading USB Device…. If it finds no partition, it shows No Partitions Found!
tl.file-manager.5: Tap a partition in the grid. To rename it, long-press it and tap Rename.
tl.file-manager.6: Browse the folders. The path at the top shows where you are.
tl.file-manager.7: How do I copy many files at once?
tl.file-manager.8: Select the files. The selection bar shows Clear Selection, Select All, Cut, Copy and Delete.
tl.file-manager.9: Tap Select All to select everything in the folder, then Copy or Cut.
tl.file-manager.10: Go to the target folder and tap Paste in the toolbar.
tl.file-manager.11: To copy files out of the drive, select them and use Export in the selection menu. FAT32 cannot hold files of 4 GB or more, and the app tells you when a file hits this limit.
tl.file-manager.12: How do I add files from my phone to the drive?
tl.file-manager.13: Open the folder on the drive, tap More in the toolbar and choose Import File / Files or Import Directory. Create Directory in the same menu makes a new folder.
tl.file-manager.14: What can I do with selected files?
tl.file-manager.18: Moves or copies the files when you tap Paste in another folder.
tl.file-manager.20: Deletes the files after you confirm.
tl.file-manager.24: Copies the selected files out of the drive.
tl.file-manager.26: Shows the details of one selected item.
tl.file-manager.28: Opens the file in another app that may also save changes to it.
tl.file-manager.29: How do I find and sort files?
tl.file-manager.30: Tap Search in the toolbar (Search files). Tap Sort By to sort by Name (A–Z or Z–A), Size (smallest or largest first) or Date (oldest or newest first).
tl.file-manager.31: Can I open a file in another app without copying it?
tl.file-manager.32: Yes. Tap a file and choose the app. The file opens read-only, straight from the drive. Use Open for editing when the other app should be able to save changes. Some files open as a copy instead. APK files cannot be opened.
tl.file-manager.33: Which file systems does it open?
tl.file-manager.34: FAT12, FAT16, FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, ext2, ext3 and ext4. A drive opens here even when the phone's own file manager does not show it.
tl.file-manager.35: The drive opens read-only in three cases: when it is write-protected, when a repair it needs did not succeed, and when it did not keep its test data. In the last case the app also offers Try restore again.

tl.file-manager.38: To let other apps reach a whole partition through Android's file picker, use Partition Mounter.
tl.file-manager.39: If a file cannot be read during an import, the app skips it and copies the rest.
tl.file-manager.40: In Ventoy (Unofficial), tap USB File Manager on the Ventoy screen instead. The button works only when Ventoy is on the drive.
tl.file-manager.41: USB File Manager is also a separate app: see USB File Manager.

tl.format-usb.27: What does the app check after formatting?

tl.format-usb.44: A job never writes to a different drive than the one it started on.

tl.iso-burner.1: How do I burn an image to a USB drive step by step?

tl.iso-burner.3: Boot Selection: keep Disk or ISO image to write an image file, or choose Non-bootable, MS-DOS or FreeDOS. Changing it resets your other choices.
tl.iso-burner.4: Tap Pick ISO and choose the image. The app shows Reading ISO File and its progress while it reads the image; you can stop this with Cancel.
tl.iso-burner.5: Check ISO Label: and Size:, then the options the app shows for this image. It sets their defaults from the image.
tl.iso-burner.6: Tap START. The app shows All Data Will Be Permanently Deleted and how many tokens the burn uses. Tap OK to start.
tl.iso-burner.7: Keep the app in front until the burn finishes.
tl.iso-burner.8: DROFUS is an independent app, not affiliated with Rufus.
tl.iso-burner.9: Which options can I set, and what are the defaults?
tl.iso-burner.10: The app shows only the options that fit the chosen mode and image.
tl.iso-burner.15: Non-bootable, Disk or ISO image, MS-DOS, FreeDOS
tl.iso-burner.17: Windows installation type (images that support Windows To Go)
tl.iso-burner.18: Standard Windows Installation, Windows To Go
tl.iso-burner.20: Windows edition (Windows To Go, images with more than one edition)
tl.iso-burner.22: The first Pro or Professional edition that is not Education or Workstation, otherwise the first edition
tl.iso-burner.23: Advanced Options (Filesystem, Partition & Persistence) (Linux ISOs that can be written both ways)
tl.iso-burner.24: Off: the image is written as it is. On: the image's files are copied, and file system, partition table and persistence can be set.
tl.iso-burner.27: MBR (BIOS or UEFI-CSM), GPT (UEFI); MBR, GPT for Non-bootable

tl.iso-burner.33: The sizes allowed for the file system and drive
tl.iso-burner.34: Chosen by the app; each file system has its own default (Default Value when the app cannot choose a size). The size you pick is used.
tl.iso-burner.39: Disabled, or from 256 MB up to the space left after the main partition minus 128 MB
tl.iso-burner.46: On when phone storage has enough free space, otherwise off
tl.iso-burner.47: How do I make a Windows 10 or Windows 11 installer?
tl.iso-burner.48: Pick the Windows ISO and keep Standard Windows Installation. Check the partition table and file system the app sets from the image, choose the Windows Setup Customization options you want, and tap START. Windows 7, 8, 8.1, 10 and 11 images are supported, and official Microsoft ISOs work unmodified.
tl.iso-burner.49: Partition Table: GPT (UEFI) or MBR (BIOS or UEFI-CSM). The app preselects one from the image and locks the choice when the image allows only one.
tl.iso-burner.50: File System: FAT32 or NTFS. When the image has a file over 4 GB, tick Split image for FAT32 compatibility. in the Advanced File System card so the image fits on FAT32. Without the tick the app uses NTFS, which not every UEFI firmware accepts.
tl.iso-burner.51: The split option is shown when the image can be split, the drive is 2 TB or smaller and you are not making Windows To Go. It turns off when you change the file system away from FAT32.
tl.iso-burner.52: High-speed mode. (Recommended) uses free space in phone storage. If there is not enough, the app shows how much is required and how much is available, and START stays disabled until you turn the mode off or free up space.
tl.iso-burner.53: Which Windows Setup Customization options are there?
tl.iso-burner.54: The Windows Setup Customization card changes the Windows installer you write. It appears for Windows 10 and 11 images that have no unattend file of their own, and always for Windows To Go. Nothing you enter leaves the phone.
tl.iso-burner.58: Remove requirement for 4GB+ RAM, Secure Boot and TPM 2.0.
tl.iso-burner.61: Remove requirement for an online Microsoft account.
tl.iso-burner.67: Set regional options to the same as this device:
tl.iso-burner.79: QoL improvements (Don't force Copilot, OneDrive, Outlook, Fast Startup, etc.).
tl.iso-burner.82: Use "Windows CA 2023" signed bootloaders (Requires a compatible target PC).
tl.iso-burner.86: Windows 11 build 26200 and later, not Windows To Go
tl.iso-burner.88: When you tick Create local account., the app asks for a User name of at least 3 characters; Windows asks for the account's password at first sign-in. When you tick the "Windows CA 2023" option, the app asks you to confirm first.
tl.iso-burner.89: What is Windows To Go, and where is the option?
tl.iso-burner.90: Windows To Go puts a portable Windows 10 or 11 on the USB drive that runs from the drive itself. After you pick the Windows ISO, choose Windows To Go instead of Standard Windows Installation. The choice appears only for images that support Windows To Go, and not for a bare .wim file.
tl.iso-burner.91: If the image has more than one edition, choose the edition in the list that appears. The app preselects the first Pro or Professional edition that is not Education or Workstation.
tl.iso-burner.92: The file system is NTFS, and Set the target's internal drives offline is on by default.
tl.iso-burner.93: The app warns that Windows To Go is a very long process that may take several hours. Use a high-end phone, a high-speed USB drive and High-speed mode. (Recommended), and charge the phone fully before you start.
tl.iso-burner.94: How do I write a Linux ISO, and can I add persistence?
tl.iso-burner.95: By default the app writes a Linux ISO as it is, keeping its original layout. This uses no tokens.
tl.iso-burner.96: To choose the file system and partition table yourself, or to add persistence, tick Advanced Options (Filesystem, Partition & Persistence). The app then copies the image's files to the drive instead, which uses 2 tokens. The tick is shown only for ISOs that can be written both ways.
tl.iso-burner.97: Persistent partition size: move the slider from Disabled to add a persistent partition. It keeps your files and changes between boots.
tl.iso-burner.98: Persistence file system: ext3 or ext4. It is shown when a size is set and more than one file system is possible.
tl.iso-burner.99: Where persistence is not possible, the app shows a note instead of the slider: the image does not support it, the distribution sets it up itself, or the image is written as it is. Persistence also needs enough free space on the drive.
tl.iso-burner.100: Can I write a macOS DMG or a Raspberry Pi image?
tl.iso-burner.101: Yes. Keep Disk or ISO image and pick the file. The app writes macOS DMG images (Intel-based), Raspberry Pi OS and other ARM images as they are, with no file system or partition options. These writes use no tokens. Compressed images (.gz, .xz, .bz2 or .zip, holding one bootable disk image) are unpacked as they are written.
tl.iso-burner.102: How do I make an MS-DOS or FreeDOS drive, or just format the drive?
tl.iso-burner.103: Choose MS-DOS or FreeDOS under Boot Selection and tap START. No image file is needed. This uses 1 token.
tl.iso-burner.104: Choose Non-bootable to format the drive without making it bootable. Set Partition Table:, File System: and Cluster Size:, then tap START. This uses 1 token. It also gives back the full space of a drive after a bootable write.
tl.iso-burner.105: What does the app check before it writes?
tl.iso-burner.106: The app checks the drive and the image first, and it stops or asks you when something is wrong:
tl.iso-burner.107: Fake capacity: the app checks the drive when you connect it. If reading or writing at the end of the drive fails, it may be fake or faulty, and the app asks whether to Scan for real size or Continue anyway. A burn is never refused: if you keep the claimed size, it warns you once, with Continue and Cancel, before anything is written and before any token is used. If the drive did not keep its test data, the app says so, keeps its files read-only and offers Try restore again. A burn still runs after an extra Yes; if you answer No, the burn ends and the tokens come back.
tl.iso-burner.108: Drive cannot be used: if the app cannot read or write the drive, it shows Failed to read USB device. and asks you to reinsert the drive. The drive may be write-protected, or the cable or connector may be faulty.
tl.iso-burner.109: Drive too small: the app shows Not enough space on the drive. with the space needed and the space available. It counts the drive size minus 100 MB as available.
tl.iso-burner.110: Drives over 2 TB: MBR and FAT32 cannot be used, and the app says so.
tl.iso-burner.111: Truncated or corrupt ISO: when an ISO looks truncated or corrupted, which usually means the download was interrupted, the app says so and asks whether to continue anyway. An image that is incomplete or damaged is refused, with a message to download it again.
tl.iso-burner.112: Not bootable: the app shows The selected file is not a bootable image. and asks whether to continue anyway. A file it cannot use shows Unsupported File.
tl.iso-burner.113: File no longer there: if the image cannot be opened when you tap START, the app shows Cannot Open File.
tl.iso-burner.114: Phone storage: with High-speed mode on, the app checks the free space in phone storage first.
tl.iso-burner.115: Erase confirmation: nothing is written before you confirm All Data Will Be Permanently Deleted.
tl.iso-burner.116: How many tokens does a burn use?
tl.iso-burner.119: Disk or ISO image with the image's files copied: Windows, Windows To Go, Linux with Advanced Options
tl.iso-burner.120: Disk or ISO image written as it is: Linux without Advanced Options, macOS DMG, Raspberry Pi and other raw images
tl.iso-burner.122: The app shows the cost before it starts, and you earn a token by watching one short rewarded video. With Pro, burning uses no tokens. If you do not have enough tokens, the app shows Not Enough Tokens with a Get Tokens button, and nothing starts.
tl.iso-burner.123: The tokens come back automatically when the burn fails, is cancelled or stops with an error, and when the app is closed during the burn (they are returned the next time the app starts).
tl.iso-burner.124: How long does a burn take?
tl.iso-burner.125: It depends on the speed of the USB drive and of the phone's USB port. Turn on High-speed mode. (Recommended) when the app offers it. Windows To Go can take several hours.
tl.iso-burner.126: What happens if the burn is interrupted?
tl.iso-burner.127: Keep the app in front. When it goes to the background, Windows, Linux and raw-image burns pause, and they continue when you come back to the app while it is still running. The app keeps the screen on while it is shown.
tl.iso-burner.128: In the free version, a running burn also pauses while the phone has no internet connection or an ad blocker or blocking Private DNS is active, and continues when that is fixed. With Pro, only the background pause applies.
tl.iso-burner.129: If the drive is unplugged or stops answering, the app shows Device Removed with Retry. Plug the same drive back in and tap Retry: most burns continue where they stopped (a Windows To Go burn in normal mode repeats its image step). If you cancel instead, the tokens come back.
tl.iso-burner.130: Write-protected drive: a drive that is write-protected or does not take writes is refused at the start, with one message, before any question and before any token is used.
tl.iso-burner.131: Checking image...: before the drive is erased, the app checks the image. An image that is incomplete or cannot be read is refused, and nothing is written to the drive.
tl.iso-burner.132: File cannot be picked: the app shows Storage is not ready, or Pick the file from Internal storage, or copy it first.
tl.iso-burner.133: No BIOS boot loader: if the BIOS boot loader cannot be installed for a Linux image copied file by file, the drive is finished with the note It may start only on UEFI computers.
tl.iso-burner.134: Why did the burn fail, and what do I do?
tl.iso-burner.135: When a burn cannot finish, the message names the cause:
tl.iso-burner.137: The image is incomplete or damaged. Download it again.
tl.iso-burner.138: The WIM file cannot be split for FAT32. Choose NTFS.
tl.iso-burner.139: The drive did not keep the copy. It may be counterfeit.
tl.iso-burner.140: The drive could not be set up as NTFS. Choose FAT32 or exFAT.
tl.iso-burner.141: The phone does not have enough memory.
tl.iso-burner.142: If you plug in a different drive during a burn, the app never writes to it.
tl.iso-burner.143: It works with USB flash drives, SD card adapters and external SSDs.
tl.iso-burner.144: Modern Linux distributions released after 2010 are supported, such as Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian and Arch.
tl.iso-burner.145: Empty card reader: if there is no card in the card reader, the app says there is no card or disk in the drive.
tl.iso-burner.146: Is a burn safe for my drive?
tl.iso-burner.147: Yes. Every burn that makes a file system is tested before success is shown, and image writes wait until the drive confirms the data is written. Besides the checks above:
tl.iso-burner.148: Every burn that formats the drive checks and tests the file system before the app reports success.
tl.iso-burner.149: A burn that fails or is cancelled leaves the drive marked to be formatted again, so a half-written drive is never mistaken for a good one.
tl.iso-burner.150: If the USB connection fails for a moment during a job, the app recovers it automatically and the job continues.
tl.iso-burner.151: More than five years of building USB apps, and over 1,000,000 downloads each on Google Play for Ultimate USB and DROFUS.
tl.iso-burner.152: Read more: How our USB apps keep your drive and your data safe.
tl.iso-burner.153: This also holds when a burn is stopped by force, for example when the app is force-closed or the phone switches off, for every burn type: file copy, disk image, image in an archive, DMG, Windows To Go, MS-DOS and FreeDOS.
tl.iso-burner.desc: Open ISO Burner in Ultimate USB or DROFUS, tap Pick ISO, check the options and tap START. It writes Windows, Linux, macOS DMG and Raspberry Pi images, and can also make an MS-DOS or FreeDOS drive or just format the drive. Images written as they are use no tokens; other burns use 1 or 2.

tl.partition-image-manager.1: How do I create a new partition image?
tl.partition-image-manager.2: Open Ultimate USB, open the File & Storage group and tap Partition Image Manager.
tl.partition-image-manager.4: Enter the name, the size and its unit (MB or GB), and a volume label, and choose the file system.
tl.partition-image-manager.5: Pick the folder where the image file is saved. The app checks that there is enough free space and whether a file with that name already exists.
tl.partition-image-manager.6: The app shows Your partition is ready! Would you like to open it? Open it to add files.
tl.partition-image-manager.7: Which options can I set, and what are the defaults?
tl.partition-image-manager.12: A number of up to 3 digits; at least 40 MB
tl.partition-image-manager.17: FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, Ext2, Ext3, Ext4 (FAT16 is not offered)
tl.partition-image-manager.19: How do I open an image file and see what is inside?
tl.partition-image-manager.20: In Partition Image Manager, tap View Partition Image (.img/.bk).
tl.partition-image-manager.21: Pick the image file, then pick a partition in it.
tl.partition-image-manager.22: Browse it as you would a drive in USB File Manager: Copy, Cut, Paste, Delete, Rename, Import, Export, Search and Sort.
tl.partition-image-manager.23: This also opens a .bk backup made with Backup / Restore, so you can look inside it without restoring it to a drive.
tl.partition-image-manager.24: Does Partition Image Manager use tokens?
tl.partition-image-manager.25: No. Partition Image Manager is free.
tl.partition-image-manager.26: To write an image file to a drive, use Raw Write.

tl.partition-mounter.1: How do I mount a partition step by step?
tl.partition-mounter.2: Connect the drive to your phone with a USB OTG adapter and open Ultimate USB.
tl.partition-mounter.3: Open the File & Storage group and tap Partition Mounter.
tl.partition-mounter.7: Tap Open Files App. The system Files app opens, and the partition is there.
tl.partition-mounter.8: When you are done, tap Unmount, then unplug the drive.
tl.partition-mounter.9: Which options can I set, and what are the defaults?
tl.partition-mounter.18: If the drive refuses writes, the app mounts it read-only, even when you chose Read / Write.
tl.partition-mounter.19: Can other apps open the files on the drive?
tl.partition-mounter.20: Yes. While the partition is mounted, other apps can open its files through Android's file picker. With Read / Write, they can also save to it.
tl.partition-mounter.21: Why can't I go back or eject the drive?
tl.partition-mounter.22: While a partition is mounted, the app refuses Back and Eject and shows Unmount partition first. Tap Unmount, then go back or eject. While mounted, the partition, the mode and Mount cannot be changed; only Unmount is available.
tl.partition-mounter.25: To browse and manage files inside Ultimate USB instead, use USB File Manager.
tl.partition-mounter.desc: In Ultimate USB, open Partition Mounter, choose the partition and Read Only or Read / Write, tap Mount and Open Files App. Other apps can open the files through Android's file picker. Unmount before you unplug.

tl.partition-wizard.1: How do I change partitions step by step?
tl.partition-wizard.2: Connect the drive to your phone with a USB OTG adapter and open Ultimate USB or USB Tools.
tl.partition-wizard.3: Open the Disk Management group and tap Partition Wizard.
tl.partition-wizard.4: Tap a partition, or Unallocated Space, in the list.
tl.partition-wizard.5: Pick an action: Create, Format, Delete, Wipe, Rename, Backup, Restore or Convert. The action is added to the Changes list.
tl.partition-wizard.6: Add more actions if you need them. Undo removes the last planned change.
tl.partition-wizard.7: Tap Apply Changes. The app asks Are you sure you want to apply all changes? This operation cannot be undone. and shows how many tokens the changes use. Confirm to start.
tl.partition-wizard.8: If you leave the screen with planned changes, the app shows Unsaved Changes and asks whether you want to exit without saving.
tl.partition-wizard.13: Makes a new partition in empty space of at least 32 MB, with FAT16, FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, EXT2, EXT3 or EXT4. It uses all of the space unless you set a custom size.
tl.partition-wizard.15: Formats the partition with the file system, Cluster Size and label you choose.
tl.partition-wizard.17: Removes the partition, so its space becomes unallocated.
tl.partition-wizard.19: Erases everything on the partition and removes it.
tl.partition-wizard.21: Gives the partition a new name.
tl.partition-wizard.23: Saves the partition as an .img file named backup_ plus a number, in a folder you pick.
tl.partition-wizard.25: Writes an image file back to the partition. The file must be exactly the size of the partition.
tl.partition-wizard.27: Converts the partition table from MBR to GPT or from GPT to MBR.
tl.partition-wizard.28: Which limits does the wizard check?
tl.partition-wizard.29: The wizard stops a change that the drive cannot hold, and tells you why:
tl.partition-wizard.30: A new partition needs at least 32 MB of empty space.
tl.partition-wizard.31: An MBR drive holds at most 4 partitions. A GPT drive with more than 4 partitions cannot be converted to MBR.
tl.partition-wizard.32: FAT32 cannot handle partitions larger than 2TB and MBR cannot handle partitions larger than 2TB. Use exFAT or NTFS, or GPT, for a larger partition.
tl.partition-wizard.33: Back up the drive first with Backup / Restore: a change to a partition table is not one you want to stop halfway through.
tl.partition-wizard.34: How many tokens does Partition Wizard use?
tl.partition-wizard.35: Apply Changes uses 1 token for each Create or Format in the list, and at most 3 tokens in total. Convert, Delete, Wipe, Rename, Backup and Restore are free. The app shows the cost before it starts, and you earn a token by watching one short rewarded video. With Pro, Partition Wizard uses no tokens.
tl.partition-wizard.36: If the changes fail, the tokens for the Create and Format steps that did not finish come back. If the app is closed while the changes run, the tokens are returned the next time the app starts.
tl.partition-wizard.37: Can I stop the changes while they run?
tl.partition-wizard.38: Yes. Tap cancel and the app asks Are you sure you want to cancel the process? If the drive is unplugged while the changes run, the app reports Device Removed.
tl.partition-wizard.39: A partition that reaches past the drive's real size is marked in the list.
tl.partition-wizard.40: If a conversion from MBR to GPT is refused, the app explains why.
tl.partition-wizard.41: On a write-protected drive, only Backup runs.
tl.partition-wizard.42: Each action changes only the partition you picked.
tl.partition-wizard.43: Is Partition Wizard safe for my drive?
tl.partition-wizard.44: Yes. The app tests every new or formatted partition before it reports success, and it protects the drive at each step:
tl.partition-wizard.45: Create and Format check and test the new file system before the app reports success.
tl.partition-wizard.46: If the drive did not keep its test data, it may be fake. The app says so, keeps its files read-only and offers Try restore again.
tl.partition-wizard.47: A job never writes to a different drive than the one it started on.
tl.partition-wizard.48: If the USB connection fails for a moment during a job, the app recovers it automatically and the job continues.
tl.partition-wizard.49: More than five years of building USB apps, and over 1,000,000 downloads each on Google Play for Ultimate USB and USB Tools.
tl.partition-wizard.50: Read more: How our USB apps keep your drive and your data safe.

tl.ps2-usb-utils.1: How do I add a PS2 game step by step?
tl.ps2-usb-utils.2: Connect the drive to your phone with a USB OTG adapter and open Ultimate USB or USB Tools.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.3: Open the Gaming Tools group and tap PS2 USB Utils.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.4: At the top, check File System:, Partition Table: and Available Space:. If the drive is not FAT32 or exFAT with an MBR partition table, tap Fix first.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.5: Tap Import & Split ISO and pick an ISO or ZSO game file.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.6: Choose the Installation Method when the app asks, and start the copy.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.7: The game appears in the list. The app shows Found N game(s), or No Games Found when the drive has none.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.8: The list shows the games in ul.cfg, the PS2 ISO games in /CD and /DVD, and the PS1 games in /POPS.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.9: How do I prepare the drive for OPL with Fix?
tl.ps2-usb-utils.10: Fix is available when the drive is not FAT32 or exFAT, or when its partition table is not MBR. What it does depends on the drive:
tl.ps2-usb-utils.11: If the file system is not FAT32 or exFAT, the drive does not have exactly one partition, or the partition is larger than MBR allows, the app formats the drive. Choose FAT32 or exFAT; the label is PS2 unless you change it. The app shows All Data Will Be Permanently Deleted and the token cost before it starts. The drive gets an MBR partition table, and the partition is limited to the MBR maximum size.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.12: If the drive already has one FAT32 or exFAT partition that fits, the app only rewrites the partition table as MBR. It does not format, your files stay on the drive, and it uses no token.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.13: Should I use Direct Copy or split the game to UL?
tl.ps2-usb-utils.14: Use Direct Copy - Recommended when the app offers it. The choice appears when the game file is smaller than 4 GB, or when the drive is exFAT. A game of 4 GB or more on a drive that is not exFAT is always split into USBExtreme (.ul) parts, and ul.cfg is updated.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.27: The game name is taken from the file name, cut to 31 characters, with characters that Windows does not allow in file names removed. A direct copy goes to /CD when the image fits the CD size, otherwise to /DVD.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.28: CSO files are refused with Unsupported File. Convert them to ISO or ZSO first with Game Converter. If an image is not complete, the app says This image is incomplete. Download it again.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.29: How do I import a game that is already in .ul format?
tl.ps2-usb-utils.30: Tap Import .ul game and pick the folder. If the folder holds ul.* parts or a ul.cfg, the app imports the UL game. Otherwise it offers the .iso and .zso files in that folder.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.31: How do I add PS1 games for POPStarter?
tl.ps2-usb-utils.32: Tap Import VCD Game and pick a .VCD file. Only .VCD files are accepted. The app then shows Copying image…, Writing launcher… and Updating conf_apps.cfg…. It creates the launcher /POPS/XX.<name>.ELF.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.33: The name may use letters, numbers, spaces, dots, hyphens and underscores. The launcher path can be up to 89 characters.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.34: A game with the same name already in /POPS is refused.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.35: On FAT32, a .VCD file of 4 GB or more is refused. The app also checks that there is enough free space.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.36: The app warns you when the drive uses GPT.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.37: POPStarter needs a system file (POPS_IOX.PAK) that the app does not include; you supply it yourself. While it is missing, the app shows Setup incomplete. Tap the banner, and in One step remains tap Select file to add it.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.38: How do I rename, delete, export or tidy up games?
tl.ps2-usb-utils.43: Asks Enter New Name and renames the game.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.46: Asks you to confirm, then removes the game.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.49: Copies the game to a folder you pick. The app warns when the target is FAT32 and the file is 4 GB or more.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.52: Exports the game as a compressed ZSO file.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.53: A UL game or an ISO game in /CD or /DVD is selected
tl.ps2-usb-utils.55: Defragments the game files. If nothing needs it, the app says No fragmented files found.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.56: The drive is FAT32 or exFAT
tl.ps2-usb-utils.58: Deletes the leftover parts of copies that did not finish. Complete games that are not in the list are kept.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.61: Rebuilds ul.cfg and reports how many games it found.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.63: OPL needs game files that are not fragmented. If a game shows Fragmented, tap Defragment. If the app reports Quick Defragmentation Failed, tap Run Full Defragmenter.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.64: On a write-protected (read-only) drive, the app refuses every action that writes to the drive.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.65: How do I download game covers?
tl.ps2-usb-utils.66: Tap Download Game Arts and choose What to download: Artwork and game info or Artwork only. This needs an internet connection. A game with an unusual or renamed game ID may have no artwork to match.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.67: Does PS2 USB Utils use tokens?
tl.ps2-usb-utils.68: Only Fix uses a token, and only when it formats the drive: 1 token. The app shows the cost before it starts, and you earn a token by watching one short rewarded video. Adding, exporting, renaming, deleting games and downloading covers use no tokens. With Pro, Fix uses no tokens.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.69: The token comes back when the drive is gone after you confirm, when you decline the prompt to overwrite the whole drive, when the format fails or stops with an error, and when the job is cancelled or the app is closed (it is returned the next time the app starts).
tl.ps2-usb-utils.70: Does the app include PS2 or PS1 games?
tl.ps2-usb-utils.71: No. The app organises game files you already own. It does not include game images, BIOS files or console firmware.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.72: With Artwork and game info, the game info is saved in CFG/<ID>.cfg, where <ID> is the game ID. A CFG file that is already on the drive is never replaced.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.73: Fix stays off when another volume on the drive was not closed properly.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.74: After Rename or Delete, the app tells you what the drive did. If a job stops at a bad sector, the app offers Check the drive.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.75: Is PS2 USB Utils safe for my drive?
tl.ps2-usb-utils.76: Yes. The app tests every format before it reports success, and it protects the drive at each step:
tl.ps2-usb-utils.77: When Fix formats the drive, it checks and tests the new file system before the app reports success.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.78: If the drive did not keep its test data, it may be fake. The app says so, keeps its files read-only and offers Try restore again. Fix still formats the drive after an extra Yes; if you answer No, the token comes back.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.79: A job never writes to a different drive than the one it started on.
tl.ps2-usb-utils.80: If the USB connection fails for a moment during a job, the app recovers it automatically and the job continues.

Games are copied directly or split into USBExtreme (.ul) parts. It also imports PS1 .VCD games for POPStarter. Only a Fix that formats uses a token.
